claim: ZeRO's total communication volume is 3M per step, spread over two all-gathers and one reduce-scatter.
stance_target: the 3Psi / 1.5x-vs-DDP communication multiplier, corroborated independently by ZeRO++
quoted_support: In total, ZeRO has a total communication volume of 3M, spreads evenly across 2 all-gather and 1 reduce-scatter.

claim: ZeRO++ reduces ZeRO's communication volume by 4x, enabling up to 2.16x better throughput at 384-GPU scale.
stance_target: the claim that FSDP's 1.5x multiplier is not a fixed floor and can be engineered down on slow fabrics
scope_conditions: Up to 384 GPUs; low-bandwidth and small-per-GPU-batch regimes
quoted_support: Collectively, ZeRO++ reduces communication volume of ZeRO by 4x, enabling up to 2.16x better throughput at 384 GPU scale.

claim: Per-GPU throughput on low-bandwidth clusters is only half of that on high-bandwidth clusters.
stance_target: the claim that fabric bandwidth, not FLOPs, sets the achievable training throughput on this box
scope_conditions: Clusters with sub-100 Gbps cross-node links vs NVLink/NVSwitch clusters
quoted_support: As shown in Figure 1(a), the per GPU throughput on low bandwidth clusters is only half of that with high-bandwidth clusters.

claim: Cross-node links in most cloud environments are under 100 Gbps Ethernet, making them the communication bottleneck even when intra-node NVLink is fast.
stance_target: the claim that the slowest link in the hierarchy governs training throughput, which on a PCIe-only box is every link
scope_conditions: Cloud clusters with DGX-class nodes and Ethernet cross-node links
quoted_support: Although high performance nodes like DGX boxes are equipped with high-bandwidth NVLink and NVSwitch as intra-node interconnects, cross-node links are often less than 100Gbps ethernet which makes it the communication bottleneck.

claim: qwZ quantizes weights from FP16 (2 bytes) to INT8 (1 byte) before the forward all-gather, halving that collective's volume, with block-based quantization to preserve accuracy.
stance_target: the claim that bf16/fp8 collectives are the cheapest lever for cutting FSDP communication on a slow fabric
quoted_support: we adopt quantization on weights to shrink down each model parameter from FP16 (2 bytes) to INT8 (1 byte) data type before communicating, thus reducing the communication volume by half.

claim: hpZ keeps a full model copy inside each machine and replaces the cross-machine backward all-gather with an intra-machine all-gather, trading GPU memory for bandwidth.
stance_target: the claim that hierarchical (node-local) sharding is the right structure when inter-node links are slow - and that on a 5-GPU single-node box this optimization is moot
scope_conditions: Multi-node clusters with a fast intra-node tier
quoted_support: instead of spreading whole model weights across all the machines, we maintain a full model copy within each machine. At the expense of higher memory overhead, this allows us to replace the expensive cross-machine all-gather on weights with intra-machine all-gather

claim: qgZ replaces the reduce-scatter with an all-to-all-based quantized gradient averaging because naive quantization of reduce-scatter accumulates and amplifies error.
stance_target: the caveat that gradient quantization interacts badly with reduction, which matters for any bf16/fp8 gradient sync on this box
quoted_support: Directly applying quantization to reduce communication volume is infeasible. The main issue is, even by incorporating block-based quantization to reduce-scatter operation, it will still significantly hurt model training accuracy. The key reason behind is quantization will decrease value precision. And reduction on low-precision values will accumulate and amplify the errors.

claim: ZeRO++ reports consistent speedups of up to 2.4x over ZeRO and over 45% of sustained peak throughput on models up to 384 GPUs.
stance_target: the achievable MFU band for communication-optimized sharded training
quoted_support: like models on up to 384 GPUs achieving over 45% of sustained peak throughput, ii) consistent speedup of up to 2.4x over ZeRO

claim: Even on high-bandwidth clusters, running on thousands of GPUs forces a very small batch per GPU because global batch cannot grow indefinitely without hurting convergence, which reduces the compute-to-communication ratio.
stance_target: the claim that a 5-GPU box with a 1M-token global batch is in the opposite regime - large per-GPU batch, favorable compute-to-communication ratio
scope_conditions: Thousands of GPUs, convergence-limited global batch size
quoted_support: as global batch size cannot be increased indefinitely without slowing down model convergence, training on thousands of GPUs forces the batch size per GPU to be very small, which reduces the compute-to-communication ratio
